title: Newer-than-supported config rejected with clear error
command_run: printf "version: 99\n" > config.yaml; loom serve --port 8097 (then loom config migrate)
actual_result: loom serve SILENTLY accepts version: 99 — starts up with 0 workspaces (falls back to empty). No rejection, no error on startup. Separately, loom config migrate CLI does reject with the expected error.
expected_result: loom serve should refuse to start and print error message
log_evidence: loom serve log: normal startup, total_workspaces=0. loom config migrate: Error: config version 99 is newer than supported version 2; please upgrade loom. EXIT=1
notes: BUG: autoMigrateFile in internal/cli/config/config_migrate.go:147 returns rawBytes unchanged when origVersion >= CurrentConfigVersion. Serve path then loads empty config instead of rejecting. Config file correctly remains at version: 99 (not rewritten). Gate-check only works for the loom config migrate CLI command, not for loom serve. Filing follow-up ticket.

title: Destructive migrations require explicit loom config migrate

actual_result: No migrations currently have Destructive: true (migrations v0->v1 and v1->v2 both default Destructive: false). AutoMigrateConfigData at config_migrate.go:80 explicitly checks m.Destructive at line 90 and stops before applying it. Code path confirmed.
expected_result: Destructive steps skipped unless loom config migrate invoked
log_evidence: N/A - code inspection
notes: Framework is in place (Migration.Destructive field, AutoMigrateConfigData skip logic). No current migration is flagged destructive, so test is theoretical. Verified AutoMigrateConfigData:90 halts chain when m.Destructive==true; MigrateConfigData (invoked by loom config migrate) applies all regardless.

title: loom config migrate --dry-run reports pending migrations without writing
command_run: sha256sum config.yaml; loom config migrate --dry-run; sha256sum config.yaml; diff
actual_result: File HASH CHANGED — dry-run modified the file. Auto-migration happened before runConfigMigrate executed. Output: "auto-migrated config path=... from_version=0 to_version=2 / Config is already at version 2, no migration needed." — the dry-run path never got a chance to list pending migrations.
expected_result: File byte-identical pre/post; stdout lists migration descriptions
log_evidence: pre hash: 4c747b3c... post hash: b3252989... (differs). Log shows auto-migration happened during PersistentPreRunE -> ResolveAndSetBackend -> config.LoadConfig -> autoMigrateFile
notes: BUG: rootCmd.PersistentPreRunE (root.go:121) calls ResolveAndSetBackend -> config.LoadConfig (backend.go:95) which triggers autoMigrateFile before runConfigMigrate runs. So by the time --dry-run is evaluated, non-destructive migrations have already been applied. Filing follow-up. Dry-run is effectively only useful for previewing destructive migrations (none exist currently).

title: Migration is atomic — crash mid-migration leaves old file intact
command_run: 20-iteration loop: start loom config migrate, kill -9 within 20ms, verify YAML parseable
actual_result: All 20 iterations left a parseable YAML file. Zero failures. No orphan .tmp files found. autoMigrateFile uses atomicfile.WriteFile (temp + rename) at internal/atomicfile/atomicfile.go:37.
expected_result: Every iteration leaves parseable YAML
log_evidence: FAIL=0/20. atomicfile.go: tempfile in same dir + os.Rename ensures atomicity
notes: Migrations run so fast (<20ms) that kill -9 rarely catches mid-write. But atomic semantic is proven by source: either temp rename succeeds (new content visible) or fails (old content preserved).

title: Concurrent auto-migration serialized by configlock flock
command_run: Start two loom serve processes on ports 8100/8101 in parallel against v1 config; wait 3s; inspect
actual_result: Final file version: 2. Exactly one auto-migrated log line (in server B). Server A saw already-migrated file via flock serialization.
expected_result: Final file v2; exactly one migration log line across both processes
log_evidence: A log: 0 auto-migrated lines. B log: 1 auto-migrated line. Total: 1
notes: configlock.WithLock / configlock.ConfigLock in config.go:170,264 serialize access. The race is won by one process, the other sees v2 on retry.
